passage: Diwali eve. Rafiq and the others wanted to try a firecracker trick behind the water tank, with no grown-ups. I said, "Not for me." They kept at it: "Chicken, come on, you only watch." I said no again, louder. My hands were cold. Then I turned around and walked to the front, where Papa and the neighbours were setting out the flowerpots. I told Papa quietly what they were planning. He went straight to the back with Rafiq's uncle. I stood there feeling odd, like a tattletale and a hero at once. The trick did not happen. Maybe I lost a friend for tonight. But nobody got hurt. Swati

qa.a: Swati went to the front, where Papa and the neighbours were setting out flowerpots.

qa.q: How did Swati feel after telling Papa?
qa.a: Mixed, like a tattletale and a hero at once, and unsure about losing a friend for the night. 🤔

qa.a: Swati could explain the worry about safety and suggest enjoying the festival together with adults around, because it keeps the friendship.

qa.q: How might Rafiq feel when the adults arrived?
qa.a: Caught out and annoyed at losing the trick, and perhaps a little relieved once the pressure was gone.

grounding: Swati, when the group keeps insisting on a firecracker trick, walks away and tells the adults, choosing safety over staying in the group.

passage: On the second night of Diwali, the children gathered behind the panchayat hall with a bag of crackers. Kiran had a new trick with a bomb cracker and a steel tumbler. "Sarita, you hold the matchbox and light it." Sarita shook her head. "It'll hit somebody." "Don't be a baby. Just once." They kept at it, and Kiran pushed the matchbox into her hand. Sarita put it down on the wall, turned around and walked straight to the courtyard where the grown-ups were drinking tea. "Kiran is going to blow a tumbler up with a bomb," she told her Chachi. Chachi was up at once, calling Kiran's uncle. By the time they reached the hall, the tumbler was taken away and the bag of crackers was in Chachi's arms.

qa.q: Where were the grown-ups when Sarita went to them?
qa.a: They were in the courtyard, drinking tea.

qa.q: What was Sarita feeling when the others kept pushing the matchbox on her?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and scared that someone would get hurt, and firm enough to put the matchbox down instead of giving in.

qa.q: Why did going to the grown-ups work better than arguing longer?
qa.a: Arguing only kept the pressure going; an adult could actually stop the trick, and Chachi took the tumbler and the crackers away that same night.

qa.q: How might Kiran see Sarita afterwards?
qa.a: Kiran may feel annoyed or embarrassed at first about losing the crackers, but might later see that Sarita kept someone from getting hurt.

grounding: Shows a girl leaving a group that keeps pushing a firecracker trick and going to the adults for safety.

passage: At twenty to midnight on New Year's Eve, the courtyard of the apartment block in Leipzig smelled of smoke. Elif and three other kids had found a box of bangers someone had left by the bins. "We light one and throw it at the very last second," Elif said, grinning. "Olga, you're the fastest. You do it." "No. People lose fingers like that." "Come on, it's New Year. Everyone does it." Elif held out the lighter again, and the others started chanting her name. Olga backed away, pulled open the heavy door and ran up two flights to the party in the Novak flat. Her mother and Mr Novak came straight down. The box went into Mr Novak's coat pocket, and the kids watched the midnight rockets from the balcony instead, with the grown-ups.

qa.a: She ran up two flights to the party in the Novak flat.

qa.q: How can you tell Olga felt under pressure when the chanting started?
qa.a: She backed away and ran for the door, which shows she felt frightened and cornered, but she chose her own safety over staying with the group.

qa.q: Which other approach could Olga have tried first, and would it have been enough?
qa.a: She could have suggested watching the rockets together instead, but with the lighter held out and the chanting going, getting adults was the surer way to stop anyone getting hurt.

qa.q: What is the rest of New Year's Eve like for Elif after the grown-ups arrive?
qa.a: Elif loses the exciting plan and may feel sulky, but still gets to watch the midnight rockets, safely, from the balcony.

grounding: Shows a girl walking away from friends who keep insisting on a firecracker trick and fetching adults.
